items.title: Show HN: SPEV: Open Weight, Omnimodal Decision Model Trained for Turn Detection (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Where Jev and other Jev-style models like OpenAI's Decisions and Cloudflare's Clef are multimodal, supporting text or images in, decision out, SPEV natively supports audio and video inputs. These native capabilities allow SPEV to reason directly from audio without the lossy speech to text conversion caused by transcription enabling audio capabilities like agent turn detection. SPEV also achieves substantial latency improvements on audio tasks compared to other decision models by skipping the transcription step and operating directly on the raw audio. In our benchmarks SPEV returns an audio native decision in 166 ms compared to 752 ms from OpenAI after including the transcription roundtrip. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50089639 Points: 2 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: VS Code Bridge for Claude Code (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: I use Claude Code inside VS Code, and four things kept getting in my way: 1. I couldn't send Claude my Markdown Editor selection, or a file I had open as a preview. 2. The claude CLI got none of the editor's context. 3. Claude couldn't run VS Code commands, so it couldn't adapt VS Code to what I was doing. 4. File links in its chat ignored the editor I chose for the file type and opened as raw text (https://github.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/81482). So I wrote an extension and a Claude Code plugin that fix those. It turned out useful enough to share. Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50089454 Points: 1 # Comments: 0

items.title: Show HN: A guided 3D Leonardo da Vinci museum, built in code (Source: hnrss.org | Category: Hacker News)
items.content_text: Hello HN, I am the founder of a small nonprofit which built Museum of Ages. We opened its first wing last week, a digital Leonardo da Vinci museum. It is a virtual tour with 17 stops, his works and then his last house in Amboise. The entrance is free. At the different stops you can see for example his paintings close to their real size, or 15 of his machines rebuilt in code, and you can have a look at 29 of his anatomy sheets. We also selected 207 of his manuscript pages which you can read in a virtual reading table, mirror the view to read his writing and 131 of the 207 are translated. We also rebuilt his last house in Amboise on the later stops of the walk. The museum is available in seven languages. Each stop has one of four grades as a label, documented, reconstructed, conjectural and not known. In a detailed view the user can have a closer look at the sources. The materials of the rooms and machines are created in Three.js. The museum runs with WebGPU. If the browser doesn't support it, the fallback is WebGL2. To create the textures we used Creative Commons Zero photo scans (CC0) and for a few small objects we use free 3D models (CC0). Our mission is to create digital museums you can walk as not everyone can get to a museum, because illness or disability keeps them away. Some cannot afford the trip or just reside far away. So our goal is also to make our digital museums as accessible as possible. Therefore we also pre-rendered the walk so that it also works on older phones and is easy to use for older people. We released the code under AGPL-3.0. The texts and pictures are CC BY-SA 4.0. Reproductions have their own licenses. https://github.com/chipmates/museumofages We put a lot of time and passion into the museum and hope you like it. We are happy about any feedback. Which digital museum would you like to see next? Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50085022 Points: 60 # Comments: 27

items.content_text: Guitoro is a free browser guitar using recordings of real instruments. You can strum with your keyboard, mouse, or touchscreen, choose acoustic, classical, electric guitar or bass, and see chord fingering and each stroke. Song practice can be slowed to 20%, and there are free chord tools and tuners. No signup or download. 1 minute video demo: https://youtu.be/DtcluMLdSgs I would love feedback on how the strumming feels and sounds.
